title: The four-colour Rado number of 5(x-y) = 4z is 741
statement: Every 4-colouring of {1,...,741} contains a monochromatic solution of 5(x-y) = 4z, and some 4-colouring of {1,...,740} avoids one. So R_4(5(x-y)=4z) = 741.

formal.statement: (assert (and (forall-colourings 741 4 (exists-mono-solution (= (* 5 (- x y)) (* 4 z)))) (exists-colouring 740 4 (no-mono-solution (= (* 5 (- x y)) (* 4 z))))))

evidence.notes: A complete adaptive cube cover of F_741: 6241 cubes, every one refuted, every DRAT proof re-derived by axeyum's own backward checker; covered measure exactly 4294967296/4294967296. Lower side is a replayed 4-colouring of [740].

notes:
The `computed` case: the proposition is the fact, and the existing claim ledger entry is its evidence rather than a competing record.

external_status `open`: no published value for this Rado number existed when we computed it -- the backing claim carries novelty: "new". Paired with our `computed`, that is what the validator reports as NOVEL, and it is the only status pair that says so.

Since 2026-09-04 this proposition has a formal home: `Nat.Rado` (`crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/rado.rs`, ADR-1596) defines `Sol a b x y z := a*x = a*y + b*z`, `IsColouring`, `MonoSol`, `Arrows` and `IsRadoNumber a b k n`, so the value above is now a value OF a defined object rather than a bare number. The status stays `computed`, because a definition of the object is not a proof of the value.

The residue is measured rather than assumed, and it is NOT the unary numeral: `nat_prelude::rado_tests::the_statement_at_the_ledgers_own_constant_type_checks` builds this fact's statement in the kernel and infers its type, at the same budget as every other test in that file. Unary numerals are cheap to FORM; the superlinear cost is in reduction, which a Prop that merely mentions a numeral does not do. What is missing is the proof term. `Nat.Rado.isRadoNumber_of_succ` names exactly what a certificate would have to hand over -- `Arrows a b k (succ m)` and `Arrows a b k m -> False`, with `m` a variable -- and `F:rado-r2-schur-two` is that route carried out end to end at `a = b = 1, k = 2, n = 5`. For this row both halves came from search (b = 4 sits outside Chang-De Loera-Wesley's gcd / a >= b+2 hypotheses, so the a-adic valuation colouring does not give the lower bound either), and the cube cover's 6,241 refuted cubes are the object a kernel term would have to replay.
